decided.t: Meetings always eject — ties eject everyone tied
decided.d: A meeting that reaches the vote can no longer end with nobody out. The Four Corners vote loses its dead-centre skip: every corner is a name and everyone stands in one, largest corner wins, and a tie ejects EVERY tied nominee. No seconded name by the end of nominations and the finder of the body picks one. Ejections still never tick the death board, so the price of a meeting is live taskers, not threshold — night one's problem was a silent room, and this makes silence the expensive option. The companion enforces it: the desk records one tap per ejected name (Crewmate / IMPOSTER, +1:00 each) and cannot close a meeting with none recorded; a mis-called meeting is backed out of during the gather, or by the Game Master's Undo.

systems.name: Scoring model
systems.does: PROPOSAL — replace 'every crewmate reaches 10' with an aggregate team target of 100 crew points, pooled, living + dead.
materials: Whiteboard column for CREW POINTS beside the death count
printables: Cards change from 'MY TOTAL ___ / 10' to 'MY POINTS ___' + 'Team goal: 100 — keep going past 10'
open: Target is now a spoken number, not a printed one. Cards total 11, so the dial runs 6 (easy) to 11 (every task on the card)
3 mediums + 2 easies = 8. So any target of 8 or below leaves the hard task skippable and preserves the anti-jam slack; 9 or above makes the hard task mandatory on all 16 cards
At 11 there is no slack at all — a jammed station locks a student out, which is exactly what the playbook's §7 slack was designed to prevent. Treat 10 as the practical ceiling
Answer sheet has a TONIGHT'S TARGET blank at the top of both pages so all four counselors are working from the same number

systems.name: The clock
systems.does: PROPOSAL — there is no doom timer. One stopwatch counts down from 8:00 of floor time, started when the 60-second button lock expires. Only meetings pause it. When a Sabotage resolves, if the display reads over 5:00, set it to 5:00. Ejections reset nothing.
printables: Central Command clock card
open: One stopwatch counting down from 8:00 of floor time, started when the first 60 seconds are up
Only meetings pause it. Sabotage does not pause it. Body transit does not pause it
Sabotage succeeds +1:00 · Sabotage fails −1:30 and +2 deaths
There is no doom timer. If no Sabotage fires, the round ends at 8:00
REMAINING PLANNING NOTE: the real night is ~50 min, not 40 — 8:00 floor plus 2-3 paused 3-minute meetings is 15-18 min per round. Cap meetings at 2 per round, or publish 50-55 min

systems.name: Emergen-C, bodies & ghosts

materials: Desk bell — now just Central Command's attention-getter, optional
printables: Optional: 20 small BODY floor cards, if you want a printed marker instead of the spoon
open: Benson's call, and it closes the hole cleanly: every kill produces a body, every body produces a meeting. The 60-second get-up rule and the whole unreported-death problem are gone
COST: a ghost lying on the floor for two minutes has that much less origami time, and they need 3-4 folds to clear a target of 8
SAFETY LINE for the role cards: bodies lie against a wall, never in a doorway and never on stairs. This matters most during Sabotage, when the lights are dim
Keep 'no kills in the first 60 seconds' so the round starts clean
Budget 2-3 meetings per round — each is a 3-minute hard stop that pauses the clock
Every meeting ejects at least one player — there is no skip corner and no 'nobody goes'. A tie ejects everyone tied, so a split room can empty three students into the dead room at once

systems.name: Sabotage: Lights Out
systems.does: Supply Run. Six props live at fixed doors. An imposter taps any counselor; lights dim; Central Command reads five props AND their doors, one item per person. Two minutes.
printables: 6 supply prop cards, 2 per page (FUSE U1 · BATTERY U2 · KEYCARD U4 · O2 TANK D1 · WRENCH D2 · REACTOR ROD D3)
1-page Central Command script
open: Naming the DOOR as well as the item turns it from a search problem into a scatter problem — 6th graders fail searches under a clock but win footraces
One item per person, five items from five different people. That clause is what makes the list impossible for one student to satisfy
Three pre-built call sets on the CC page, each guaranteed to span both floors so you never have to work it out mid-event
Fail = +2 deaths and −1:30, NOT an instant round loss. Against a threshold of 6, two failures put imposters at 4 without a single kill
Succeed = +1:00 on the round clock
2 per round, none in the first 2 minutes, any counselor can be tapped
Each prop has its own door printed on it, so reset is handing them to 5 students — no adult chore and nothing to remember
OPTIONAL for round 2 only: let imposters carry off one prop as sabotage. Held back because if a hidden prop gets named, failure is automatic and the crew never learns why

printables: role-cards.pdf — 5 pages, plus 3 extra copies of page 5
answer-sheet.pdf x4 copies
